identity.title: The Uncounted Crew
identity.question: Can a generation that refuses to be counted learn to give back the water before the water is owed, and what does the valley record when it does?
identity.pressure: The labour gap of the Long Return: the pulse needs trained channel hands before its date. The maintenance lineages hold the repair skill under the Special Draw Right, and the Brightwater cohort believes abundance needs no work.

author_fixed_context.story_vision_excerpt:
The Spring Ledger is a long-form fantasy Series exploring a shared water commons, the institutions that govern it, the meanings attached to obligation, and the consequences of changing collective practices. Its identity should preserve wonder, discovery, everyday belonging, meaningful relationships, institutional transformation, material consequences, and the possibility of hopeful flourishing. Do not turn it into a generic escalating-villain epic.

Experience brief: Wonder, discovery, meaningful adventure, everyday belonging, emotionally consequential relationships and an ultimately hopeful p

series_constraints.title: Finale Alternative A (not chosen)
series_constraints.summary: Noncoercive coordination by mutual dependence: gate dependence, pair-hands, a care floor, and a Gate Table with no record authority. Draw is decoupled from hands; care is counted and nothing is owed. Failure modes: correlated shock, lowland draw left unhanded, and surveillance of the tally.

series_constraints.title: Finale Alternative B (not chosen)
series_constraints.summary: An allotted binding rota for the rebuild window, with lot-drawn one-cycle Table seats, a sunset, a care floor, and grain-labour from the Compact. Hands are owed in proportion to draw, and inside the window a shortfall is a deficit to repay, not a cut in water. Failure modes: standing power through schedule, and the Hall's custody returning under another name.

series_constraints.title: Finale Alternative C (not chosen)
series_constraints.summary: Ratified in Books 27-29: normal seasons follow Alternative A, and a published Balance Stones threshold activates Alternative B's rota for a fixed window. The valley chooses the rule before the threshold is crossed. Failure modes: the threshold becomes an authority, activation by the Reading Hall's reading may be unchecked, ratification fails in calm years, and the gauge is disputed.

series_constraints.title: Ledger engine
series_constraints.summary: Recorded shares set the draw. Credit can be falsified or favoured (Book 1), opened to public access (Book 5), traded (Book 6), re-read as gift or contract (Book 15), and from Book 20 partly set by hands owed. Each change alters who must return labour.

series_constraints.title: Old Hand engine (interpretive legitimacy)
series_constraints.summary: Readings of the First Stones change what a share is: debt (Stone Hall), gift (Terrace Council) or contract (Mill Compact). A reading changes whether returns are recorded and therefore the balance on the Source.

series_constraints.title: Source engine (physical commons)
series_constraints.summary: The spring's balance follows the gap between draw and return. Thinning leaves channels dry and floods wild water below; surfeit brings stagnant pools and fever. It responds to balance rather than to any character's intention. Its deep-store pulse, the Long Return, is predicted from Book 23 and arrives in Book 30.

series_constraints.title: Gate Table
series_constraints.summary: A rotating inter-community body formed in Book 22 to set the Hollow Gate schedule from the gauge reading. Seats for each practice, and one seat drawn by lot from households without lineage craft. It holds power over the schedule only, with no authority over the record, the shares or any practice.

series_constraints.title: Maintenance lineages
series_constraints.summary: Old maintenance lineages (Ysa Trant's) who carry channel-maintenance skill from Books 9-11. From Book 20 they hold a Special Draw Right, conditional on training apprentices from outside the lineage. Working design: revocable by the Council. Whether it stays revocable is open question 5.

series_constraints.title: Mill Compact
series_constraints.summary: Lowland grain-buyers who purchase shares once records open. Their purchased draw carries no return labour. They pursue contract-debt and trade interests from outside the valley and have their own Book 27-29 bid.

series_constraints.title: Reading Hall
series_constraints.summary: Founded after the full reading in Book 15 to make the First Stones publicly readable. Keeps the public record and its readings. Publishes the Gate gauge reading (Book 22) and the Balance Stones (Book 23). It has no authority over the schedule.

series_constraints.title: Stone Hall (Reckoners)
series_constraints.summary: Hereditary keepers of the Ledger. Under this working path the Hall splits in Book 5, as the original has it, and a remnant under Keeper Corrow continues as a dissenting institution. Typed as other because v2 has no institution category.

series_constraints.title: Everyday belonging
series_constraints.summary: The warmth of shared labour and meals, which the series must keep specific across generations.

series_constraints.title: Consequential loss
series_constraints.summary: Grief and anger that follow from changed standing: those once credited lose standing, and those once uncounted gain it. From Book 20, those whose draw is cut for hands they cannot return also lose standing.

series_constraints.title: Wonder at a responsive order
series_constraints.summary: The reader's sense that the valley's order is larger and more responsive than any institution assumed.

series_constraints.title: The Hollow Gate
series_constraints.summary: The sluice that divides the high cistern's release between the upper and lower channels. The Council has set its schedule since the Turn. In the Book 15 trial the high cistern showed surfeit. The Source responds to the balance between draw and return, and surfeit is too much return, or stored water with no draw. The construction assumes that the trial's uncounted return exceeded the draw the Turn counted, so the surplus showed in the high cistern. The original does not name this mechanism, and the author may reject it. Release draws the cistern down and cannot raise it. The schedule is the object of the Book 21 conflict.

series_constraints.title: The Long Return (pulse)
series_constraints.summary: A deep-store pulse in Book 30, predicted by the Balance Stones cut in Book 23. It needs channel labour before its date and a Gate schedule that routes it. The routing decides which channel takes the surge, and that choice belongs to the valley.

series_constraints.title: The Lowfen channel
series_constraints.summary: The lower channel that carries Lower Ammen's wells. It breaks in the thaw of Book 19 and is rebuilt by lineage crews in Book 20. Its lowest terrace is where a declined share runs wild.

series_constraints.title: The gift practice (Lower Ammen)
series_constraints.summary: Labour given without a count, from the one-season Unmeasured Return in Book 15 onward. It keeps the lower channels working by release at need, and it depends on the Gate for that release.

series_constraints.title: Custody of the record
series_constraints.summary: Who holds the Ledger and on whose authority. Custody is the Stone Hall's source of legitimacy until Book 5. Public access to the credit record begins in Book 5. Custody of the master record is contested until Book 15 and plural after the Reading Hall is founded.

series_constraints.title: Hands and draw
series_constraints.summary: Who gives return labour, and who is counted for draw. This is the series' governing variable. Until Book 19 draw follows shares alone. From Book 20 it partly follows hands owed. Each finale mechanism answers the question differently.

series_constraints.title: Keeping the channels
series_constraints.summary: Who performs the return labour that keeps the spring balanced, and at what cost to families with few hands. Old lineages hold the repair skill from Books 9-11. From Book 20 lineage crews carry channel repair under a Special Draw Right, and households that can meet the rota carry the rest.

series_consequences.text: The cohort's belief is no longer uniform. The Brightwater inheritance splits into counted and uncounted practice within one generation, so plurality of practice now crosses generations as well as communities.
A capability record shows who can repair. Under the working premise a repair counts toward training only with a lineage attestation. The record does not change who is counted for draw.

The conversion's blind spot is public. The Book 20 conversion credits counted hands only, so uncounted labour by hand-light households cannot restore their draw. This makes open question 6 concrete without answering it.

The Reading Hall declines to attribute balance to persons while the Stones cannot resolve local return (P3). This matters to Alternative C's threshold and to Alternative B's deficit record, and it decides neither.
Labour readiness has begun: trained people exist where a lineage hand attests their repairs, and a visible shortfall remains.
Idrun and Hesper's relationship has changed. Continuity between them is now a matter of disagreement, not inheritance.
The three finale alternatives remain unselected. Book 24 neither chooses nor excludes any of them; each must reckon with the capability record.

later_possibilities.text: The uncounted crew may become a carrier of channel skill when the lineages end. This is a possibility, not an answer.

Any finale mechanism can draw on the capability record, but under the working premise the record also needs a lineage attestation. Pair-hands under A, rota under B and the pre-drawn panel under C each then need a lineage hand present. None of them is chosen here.
Books 25 and 26 receive two pressures: whether attestations can be withheld or favoured, and hand-light draw against the conversion, now with a concrete case.
The cohort may claim standing in coordination, for example a Gate Table seat if the author keeps the Table.
Oona's standing offer meets a valley with some hands of its own before the Book 27 to 29 bid.
A uniformly idle Brightwater generation is closed: the cohort has shown both practices.
Uncounted gift as invisible to the spring is narrowed: the Balance Stones show it in aggregate.
Quietly ignoring the Right's condition is closed: it has been tested and met provisionally.
The remnant as keeper of the labour record is closed: it offered and was declined.
The labour gap as a Book 30 surprise is closed: it is named and partly worked from Book 24.

assumptions.text: The Special Draw Right has a review point in Book 24.
assumptions.reversal: The pressure arises from the lineage's own count of the shortfall instead.

assumptions.text: The cohort reads 'nothing counted' as 'nothing owed'.
assumptions.reversal: The belief comes from invisible lineage labour alone. The function survives this.

assumptions.text: Return labour shows on the Balance Stones in aggregate, without attribution. Agent-proposed in the source; it follows from eng_source, but the Stones' resolution of local return is not established.
Gift-hands without skill can damage a channel, through the silted section. Agent-proposed in the source; no reversal is stated.
The craft-mark is a record of capability, cut by teacher and learner on the channel stone and held by no institution. Under the working premise it is not sufficient proof of training alone.
The Council accepts attested craft-marks for one review cycle. This does not decide author-reserved choice 7.
The Reading Hall refuses attribution. Agent-proposed in the source; no reversal is stated.
The remnant's custody offer and Oona's labour offer stand as described. Agent-proposed in the source; no reversal is stated.

Hesper remains a Council apprentice after the Book. This is deliberately not a statement on reform from within. The source notes that the author may instead have her leave; that is an alternative, not a stated reversal.

The Lowfen upkeep is the crew's work site. Any channel the crew can work would serve. The surge route is author-reserved, and this Book neither designates nor excludes the Lowfen. Agent-proposed in the source; no reversal is stated.

Hypothetical working premise, not canon: a craft-mark alone no longer satisfies the lineage's proof-of-training condition. The mark must also carry a lineage hand's attestation that the repair was done as taught.
assumptions.reversal: Reverse if the lineage again accepts a craft-mark alone as proof of training.

open_author_decisions.current_text: Is the Book 20 hands-to-draw conversion a lasting settlement, or a stage the finale must revisit?
Is the lineage Special Draw Right revocable or permanent, what training condition does it carry, and who carries the Turn when the maintenance lineages end? Not decided.
Which finale mechanism, A, B, C or a third, does the author choose for who gives return labour and who is counted for it? Not decided.
Does the Compact accept grain-labour in exchange for settling its claim, and does the Gate Table's schedule reach its lowland draw? Not decided.
Which channel takes the Long Return's surge, does any household flood, and does the flood cost lives or lasting losses? These are author choices and are not decided.
Is Hesper's generational motive independent of the author's preference for the Turn's sustainability? Not yet tested.
Does reform from within remain the series' stance, and does the Gate Table model it or warn against it? Not decided.
Will any terrace keep a measured ledger in Book 30, and is plurality of practice the intended end state? Not decided.
Are the Hollow Gate and the Gate Table accepted parts of the world? Not decided; both are construction additions.
Does a Balance Stones threshold exist (Alternative C), who reads it, and which body ratifies it? Not decided.
How many Brightwater shares may be drawn before the Balance Stones restrain them?
What can the high cistern physically store above its tolerance? Not established; Alternatives B and C depend on it.

function.text: Book 24 is where the Long Return's labour gap is first met by people rather than by a schedule. A generation that refuses to be counted is asked to give back the water before it is owed. The Book exercises the Old Hand, the Ledger and the Source, and exports one new kind of record: a public capability record, separate from debt, tally and aggregate balance, that says who can repair rather than who owes. Selection rationale (agent): among the candidates considered, the uncounted crew is the only one that develops the Book 23 belief locally, with a Book-length arc and closure; it uses all three engines without physics beyond P3 and P4; it puts a real choice and a real cost in a new-generation character; and its consequences bear on all three finale alternatives without favouring one.

agents.text: Hesper (named in the Book 24 source; see unk-character-sourcing) wants her generation's abundance to remain a freedom from counting. She does not want to inherit her grandmother's tally, does not convert to the Turn, and learns that the work is real while still refusing that it must be counted. The motive is designed to be judged against open question 10; whether it is independent of the author's preference is the author's decision.

The Council steward (Idrun in the source) wants the Turn humane. She needs trained hands before the date, fears gift without return, and knows what an incomplete record costs the powerless. Accepting her granddaughter's crew means accepting a gap in the tally she keeps.

Ysa Trant and the maintenance lineages: the Right is conditional on training, so they need the condition demonstrated or the Right is exposed. They guard craft standards and fear dilution by untrained gift-hands. Their stake in the review is an agent inference.

Hand-light households have drawn less since Book 20. They need draw restored. Many would rather their children's labour were counted, because the count is how the conversion gives water back. Their reasons are coherent from their side.
The best-handed houses drew most of the surplus. Counting rewards those with hands, so they want labour counted.

The Reading Hall publishes the Balance Stones and has no schedule authority. Asked to certify the crew from the Stones, it declines to attribute aggregate balance to named hands, because the Stones do not resolve local return (P3). Whether the Hall should keep any person-level record is not settled here.
The Stone Hall remnant calls uncounted labour an unrecorded debt that will default, and offers to keep the apprentices' register. The valley declines.

Oona Brisk and the Mill Compact (named in the source; see unk-character-sourcing) offer hired lowland labour if it is credited against the Compact's draw. The offer is neither accepted nor refused, because the Compact's settlement is author-reserved.

choice.text: The setting is unchanged. Hesper's third path still records capability, but a repair counts as training only when a lineage hand attests it.

options.text: Accept the count: family draw is restored, but the cohort enters the tally it refused.
Refuse: the gift stays pure, the families stay cut, and the lineage's condition stays unmet.
A third path Hesper proposes: teacher and learner each cut a mark on the channel stone. A lineage hand attests the repair, because under the working premise the mark alone is not proof of training.

costs_kept_visible.text: The craft-mark does not restore draw. The crew chooses it knowing that their own hand-light households stay cut this cycle.

Several crewmates, including the one whose terrace silted, choose to be counted instead, for their families. Hesper respects that choice, and the cohort leaves the Book split between counted and uncounted youth.
Each attested repair needs a lineage hand present at the work, so the uncounted crew is not fully independent of the lineage under the working premise.

transformation.text: Hesper moves from 'abundance needs no work' to 'the work is real and the water sees it, but people need not count it'. Under the working premise her route still needs a lineage hand's attestation, so her independence is partial. The granddaughter sets evidence against the record, and the evidence is an attested mark.

A first group of outside-lineage hands is trained through attested repairs. The size is unstated, and the group narrows the labour gap without closing it.
The Lowfen upkeep holds through the thaw, apart from the silted section, which is relaid. The source gives this without a provenance tag.
The remnant's custody offer is declined. Oona's offer stands, neither accepted nor refused.
The Book closes on the cohort's first craft-marks beside the lineage's old ones. The belonging is everyday and specific, and the wonder is quiet: the water registered what no ledger did.

# Book 24: The Uncounted Crew (architectural function)

Status: working, noncanonical. Not author-approved. Every new element is labelled **[Agent]** (agent-proposed, reversible) or **[Derived: source]**. Nothing here is author-declared. Candidate IDs refer to the W6 working candidate read through `resume` (canvas revision 10).

---

## 1. The Book's question and the pressure it develops

**Question.** *Can a generation that refuses to be counted learn to give back the water before the water is owed, and what does the valley record when it does?* [Agent]

**Pressure developed.** The labour gap of the Long Return. The pulse needs channel labour, which means trained hands, before its date (`str_long_return`, link `l_longreturn_needs_hands`). Since Book 20 the repair skill has sat with the maintenance lineages under the Special Draw Right (`inst_lineage_crews`, `th_maintenance`). The Brightwater cohort believes abundance needs no work (`ph_5_unmeasured`, Book 23). Book 24 is where the pressure is first met by people, not by a schedule. It exercises **L2** (Old Hand → Ledger → Source) and **L1** (Ledger ↔ Source), and it exports one pressure: a new kind of record, and who may trust it. [Derived: 01 §2.4 rule for development]

## 2. Why now: the inherited state it uses

- **The date is public.** The Balance Stones publish the Long Return's date and limit Brightwater's draw (`ph_5_unmeasured`; `inst_reading_hall`). Book 24 is the first Book in which the valley knows how long it has. Training takes years, so the labour question cannot wait for Books 27–29. [Derived]
- **The Right's condition.** The Special Draw Right is conditional on training apprentices from outside the lineage (`inst_lineage_crews`; `l_lineage_right_on_draw`; 01 §7). [Derived] The condition comes up for review in Book 24. [Agent]
- **The cohort's belief.** A generation that came of age after Book 20 has never seen the labour, because lineage crews do it under the Right (`th_maintenance`; 01 §3.2). [Derived]
- **Uneven abundance.** Hand-light houses have drawn less since the Book 20 conversion (`th_hands_and_draw`; `l_conversion_sets_draw`; `rx_consequence`). [Derived]
- **Hesper** led Brightwater and took a Council apprenticeship (01 §3.2). [Derived]
- **The gift reading**: "water given; hands given back; nothing counted" (`eng_old_hand`; `str_unmeasured_return`; `ph_3_old_hand`). **The Balance Stones** (`eng_source`; 01 §2.2). The Stones are the Source's public measure, cut in Book 23 and published by the Reading Hall. They do not depend on the Gate. [Derived]

Book 24 does not depend on the Hollow Gate or the Gate Table (`str_hollow_gate`, `inst_gate_table`). Their acceptance is author-reserved (01 §8.1), so the function holds whether or not the author keeps them.

## 3. The engines and how they interact

**Old Hand → Ledger (L2, first half).**
*Condition:* the cohort has inherited the gift reading as a slogan and kept only its last clause, "nothing counted". It hears this as "nothing owed". [Agent]
*Choice:* asked by the Council to supply recorded apprentices, the cohort refuses to be entered in the stewardship tally.
*Consequence:* the Right's training condition cannot be shown in the form the Council expected.
*Changed state:* the Council, the lineage and the cohort are each blocked, by their own reasons.
*New possibility:* Hesper forms a crew that will learn and work uncounted.

**Ledger → Source (L2, second half; L1).**
*Condition:* the hands-to-draw conversion credits only counted hands (`l_conversion_sets_draw`). [Derived]
*Choice:* the cohort's young from hand-light houses work uncounted.
*Consequence:* their labour improves the balance, but it cannot restore their own households' draw. Their families stay cut while the best-handed houses keep their counted advantage.
*Changed state:* the conversion's blind spot becomes visible. It sees the record, not the hands. [Agent, derived from Book 20 mechanism]
*New possibility:* the question of whether the conversion is a lasting settlement (open question 6) gains a concrete case.

**Source (balance as witness).**
*Condition:* the Source responds to balance, not to intention or record (`eng_source`). [Derived]
*Choice:* the crew keeps a stretch of the Lowfen's thaw upkeep (`str_lowfen_channel`) under Ysa Trant's instruction.
*Consequence:* the Balance Stones show the return, in aggregate. It cannot show whose hands. One badly laid section silts and must be relaid by lineage hands. [Agent]
*Changed state:* the valley sees that uncounted gift is real on the water and invisible on the record. Gift without skill also fails. This is a new physical assumption (P4), not a consequence of the caveat in 01 §2.3, which concerns gift without return and gift with unequal hands.
*New possibility:* a record of capability, rather than of hands owed.

**Ledger (a new record form).**
*Condition:* the lineage needs proof of training, the cohort refuses a count of hours, and the Council needs to know who can repair before the date.
*Choice:* the craft-mark (see §5). [Agent]
*Consequence:* the condition is met in a form that records who *can*, not who *owes*.
*Changed state:* the valley holds four kinds of record: the debt reading's ledger (remnant), the stewardship tally (care), the Balance Stones (aggregate balance) and craft-marks (capability).
*New possibility:* any finale mechanism can draw on a public record of capability. Any of them can also be undermined if that record is falsified.

## 4. Characters and institutions with independent motivations

- **Hesper Sallow** [motive Agent; derived from the cohort's Book 23 belief, which her household's burden complicates]. She wants her generation's abundance to remain a freedom from counting. She does not want to inherit her grandmother's tally. She does not convert to the Turn. She learns that the work is real while still refusing that it must be counted. Her motive is designed to be judged against open question 10 (01 §8.11). Whether it is independent of the author's preference remains the author's decision.
- **Idrun Sallow** [Derived: wants the Turn humane; Council steward]. She needs trained hands before the date. She fears gift without return, and she knows from Book 1 what an incomplete record costs the powerless. Accepting her granddaughter's crew means accepting a gap in the tally she keeps.
- **Ysa Trant and the maintenance lineages** [Derived: Right conditional on training; Agent: their stake in the review]. They need the training condition demonstrated, or the Right is exposed. They also guard craft standards and fear dilution by untrained gift-hands. Their motive is neither the Council's nor the cohort's.
- **Hand-light households** [Derived: drawn less since Book 20]. They need draw restored. Many would rather their children's labour be counted, because the count is how the conversion gives water back. They are not obstacles. Their reasons are coherent from their side (`et_cost_of_counting`).
- **The best-handed houses** [Derived: drew most of the surplus]. Counting rewards those with hands, so they want labour counted.
- **The Reading Hall** [Derived: publishes the Balance Stones, no schedule authority]. Asked to certify the crew from the Stones, it declines to attribute aggregate balance to named hands, because the Stones do not resolve local return (P3). Whether the Hall should keep any person-level record is not settled here, and B's deficit-record cost (01 §6) is unchanged. [Agent: the refusal]
- **The Stone Hall remnant** [Derived: debt reading; Corrow's survival unresolved]. It calls uncounted labour an unrecorded debt that will default, and offers to keep the apprentices' register. The valley declines. [Agent: the offer]
- **Oona Brisk and the Mill Compact** [Derived: contract claims; Book 27–29 bid]. She offers hired lowland labour if it is credited against the Compact's draw. The offer is neither accepted nor refused, because the Compact's settlement is author-reserved (01 §8.4). [Agent: the offer]

## 5. The meaningful choice and the transformation it produces

**The setting of the choice.** After the thaw, the Balance Stones show the crew's return, and the silted section has cost one hand-light household a season on its terrace. This is the household of a crewmate. [Agent: the crewmate is an unnamed agent-proposed role] The Council, through Idrun, offers to enter the crew in the stewardship tally retroactively. That would meet the Right's condition and, through the conversion, restore the hand-light families' draw.

**Hesper's choice** [Agent]. Hesper and the crew face three paths:
- accept the count (families' draw restored, but the cohort enters the tally it refused);
- refuse it (the gift stays pure, the families stay cut, and the lineage's condition stays unmet);
- take a third path that Hesper proposes.

Hesper proposes the craft-mark. When a lineage hand judges that an apprentice can perform a named repair, teacher and learner each cut a mark on the channel stone where the repair was done. The mark records capability and place. It does not record hours, does not record debt, and does not touch draw. It is public and on the water, held by no institution. [Agent; it echoes Book 1's share-marks read as evidence, `ph_1_reckoned_water`, and Book 22's separation of schedule from record, `ph_4_settled_water`]

**Its cost, kept visible.** The craft-mark does not restore draw. The crew chooses it knowing that their own hand-light households stay cut this cycle. Several crewmates, including the one whose terrace silted, choose to be counted instead, for their families. Hesper respects their choice. The cohort leaves the Book split between counted and uncounted youth.

**Transformation.** Hesper moves from "abundance needs no work" to "the work is real and the water sees it, but people need not count it". The cohort as a whole moves from one belief to two practices. Idrun moves from keeping a tally that should be complete to accepting a record she does not hold. This is a relationship across generations with emotional consequence: the granddaughter, as her grandmother did in Book 1, sets evidence against an institution's record; here the evidence is a craft-mark on the water, not a share-mark.

## 6. The local resolution

- Ysa Trant accepts craft-marks as proof of training. The Council accepts them as meeting the Right's condition **for one review cycle**. This is provisional, and it does not settle the Right's revocability or final condition (01 §8.7). [Agent]
- A first group of outside-lineage hands is trained. The size is unstated, and the group does not close the Long Return's labour gap. It shows that the gap can be narrowed. [Agent]
- The Lowfen upkeep holds through the thaw, apart from the silted section, which is relaid.
- The remnant's custody offer is declined. Oona's offer stands, neither accepted nor refused.
- The Book closes on the cohort's first craft-marks beside the lineage's old ones. The belonging is everyday and specific (`rx_belonging`, `et_belonging`), and the wonder is quiet: the water registered what no ledger did (`rx_wonder`).

## 7. Changes to the wider Series

1. **The cohort's belief is no longer uniform.** The Brightwater inheritance (01 §3.2) splits into counted and uncounted practice within one generation. Plurality of practice now crosses generations as well as communities.
2. **A capability record exists.** It is separate from the debt ledger, the tally and the Balance Stones. The Ledger engine gains a capability record, which bears on the governing variable (`th_hands_and_draw`) by showing who is able to give return labour. It does not change who is counted for draw.
3. **The conversion's blind spot is public.** The Book 20 conversion credits counted hands only, so uncounted labour by hand-light households cannot restore their draw. This makes open question 6 concrete without answering it.
4. **The Reading Hall declines to attribute balance to persons** while the Stones cannot resolve local return (P3). This matters to Alternative C's threshold and to B's deficit record, and it decides neither.
5. **Labour readiness has begun.** The Long Return preparation is no longer only a schedule. It has trained people, and a visible shortfall remains.
6. **Idrun and Hesper's relationship has changed.** Continuity between them is now a matter of disagreement, not inheritance.

## 8. Later possibilities enabled and closed

**Enabled.**
- The uncounted crew as a possible carrier of channel skill when the lineages end. This is a possibility, not an answer (01 §8.10).
- A capability record usable by any finale mechanism: pair-hands under A, rota assignment under B, the pre-drawn panel under C. It lowers some costs in each and chooses none.
- Books 25–26 pressures: whether craft-marks can be falsified or favoured (the Ledger engine at a new record, without a villain); and hand-light draw against the conversion, now with a concrete case.
- A cohort claim to standing in coordination, for example a Gate Table seat if the author keeps the Table.
- Oona's standing offer meets a valley with some hands of its own before the Book 27–29 bid.

**Closed or narrowed.**
- A uniformly idle Brightwater generation. The cohort has shown both practices.
- Uncounted gift as invisible to the spring. The Balance Stones show it in aggregate.
- Quietly ignoring the Right's condition. It has been tested and met provisionally.
- The remnant as keeper of the labour record. It offered and was declined.
- The labour gap as a Book 30 surprise. It is named and partly worked from Book 24.

## 9. Provisional assumptions

- **P1 [Agent].** The Right has a review point in Book 24. Reversal: the pressure arises from the lineage's own count of the shortfall instead.
- **P2 [Agent].** The cohort reads "nothing counted" as "nothing owed". Reversal: the belief comes from invisible lineage labour alone. The function survives this.
- **P3 [Agent].** Return labour shows on the Balance Stones in aggregate, without attribution. This follows from `eng_source`, but the Stones' resolution of local return is not established.
- **P4 [Agent].** Gift-hands without skill can damage a channel, through the silted section.
- **P5 [Agent].** The craft-mark is a record of capability, cut by teacher and learner on the channel stone, and held by no institution.
- **P6 [Agent].** The Council accepts craft-marks for one review cycle only. This does not decide author-reserved choice 7.
- **P7 [Agent].** The Reading Hall refuses attribution.
- **P8 [Agent].** The remnant's custody offer and Oona's labour offer.
- **P9 [Agent].** Hesper remains a Council apprentice after the Book. This is deliberately not a statement on reform from within (01 §8.5). The craft-mark came from a crew outside the Council, and the Council only accepted it. The author may instead have her leave.
- **P10 [Agent].** Lowfen upkeep as the crew's work site. Any channel the crew can work would serve. The surge route is author-reserved (01 §8.6). This Book neither designates the Lowfen as the surge route nor excludes it.

## 10. Alternatives considered

- **The cistern's measure.** A discovery Book that tests what the high cistern can store. It is rich in wonder, but it would settle the unresolved physical fact on which B and C depend (01 §6, §8). That would decide the finale's feasibility by physics. Rejected as a global redesign.
- **Who bears the Stones' restraint.** A dispute over how the Balance Stones' limit on Brightwater draw is shared. It is a strong L1 conflict, but it would rehearse "counted but not owed" against "owed" directly. That would pre-run A against B, and it would largely repeat Conflict A. Rejected.
- **The threshold dispute.** An early fight over reading the Stones as a trigger. It would front-load Alternative C and make the Stones an authority by Book 24. Rejected as finale-leaning.
- **An early Compact move.** Oona's bid brought forward. It would displace Books 27–29 and press on the author-reserved settlement. Reduced to a standing offer.
- **The Right's revocation.** The Council revokes or confirms the Right. That decides author-reserved choice 7. Reduced to a one-cycle provisional acceptance.

I chose the uncounted crew for four reasons. It is the only candidate that develops the Book 23 belief locally, with a Book-length arc and closure. It uses all three engines without new physics beyond P3 and P4. It puts a real choice and a real cost in a new-generation character. And it produces consequences that all three finale alternatives must reckon with without favouring one of them.

## 11. Information needed and not available

- The years between Book 24 and the Long Return, and how long a channel hand takes to train.
- The number of lineage hands and the size of the shortfall.
- Whether the Balance Stones can resolve local return at all (P3).
- Whether Corrow is alive in Book 24.
- Whether the Sallow house is hand-light. This changes the personal cost of Hesper's choice.
- What Hesper's apprenticeship involves, and what return labour consists of in normal seasons.

verbatim_source.content:
Develop a meaningful architectural function for Book 24 of The Spring Ledger.
Book 23 has transformed the next generation's understanding of the water commons.
The later Series must still confront the Long Return and unresolved questions about shared responsibility.
Construct a distinct Book 24 contribution that emerges from the inherited conditions without prematurely deciding the finale.
The Book must offer a satisfying local narrative transformation while producing consequences relevant to later Series development.
Preserve the established narrative identity, causal systems, character agency, and author-reserved choices.
